sections.h2: Where do Perry County property tax questions go?
sections.html:
Hazard holds all three offices a seller needs. The Property Valuation Administrator, called the PVA, does its appraising upstairs in the 481 Main Street courthouse, and the County Clerk keeps the ground-floor counter in that building. The Sheriff's Office, which sends and collects the bills, works from East Main Street.

  • Sheriff's tax office: 124 East Main Street; letters go to box 7309, Hazard 41702. Hours are 8:00 to 4:00 on weekdays, minus holidays. The number is 606-439-4523, option 2.
  • PVA: 606-436-4914. The sheriff's tax page links to the parcel search the PVA maintains.
  • County Clerk: 606-436-4614.

Checks to the sheriff are made payable to "Perry County Sheriff." A separate billing provider handles online payment and adds its own convenience fee.

sections.h2: What is the Perry County tax calendar?
sections.html:
The statewide schedule applies. Taxes fall due by the end of December, a 2% discount rewards payment in full by November 1, and January payments take a 5% penalty. Anything paid after January 31 carries 10% under KRS 134.015. Business on April 15 closes the sheriff's collection year. The mailing date changes yearly, so the tax office at 606-439-4523 is the place to confirm what is printed on a given bill.

The sheriff acts as collector of state, county and district taxes, and the office is paid a commission on what it collects. Late-starting years follow a slower pattern in which each stage lasts a full month.

sections.h2: How do Perry County's delinquent bills compare with the face amount?
sections.html:
Delinquency costs more each month it continues. The table below uses the Department of Revenue's own illustration of a $1,000 bill, and the sheriff's real commission rate would shift the totals a little.

Department of Revenue illustration of a $1,000 bill after it reaches the clerk
Point in the processAmount due
On transfer to the clerk, with penalty and sheriff charges$1,254.00
Settled within five business days$1,387.79
After the first county attorney letter$1,611.30
After newspaper advertising in June$1,659.90
Starting figure for an investor at the sale$1,704.21

Behind those figures are monthly interest of one percent and added clerk and attorney commissions. The clerk's sale comes 90 to 135 days after transfer. The Perry County Clerk's website points to a delinquent tax application, and the county attorney's office can set up an installment plan on a current delinquency.

sections.h2: Can a Perry County owner contest the value?
sections.html: Yes, and the route starts at the PVA's office, where the owner sits down with staff before anything is filed. The written appeal then goes to the clerk's desk by the end of the day after the thirteen-day roll inspection closes. A panel of neighbors on the local board decides, usually within five weeks, and it looks for hard evidence such as appraisals, repair bids and nearby sales.

sections.h2: Does the homestead exemption apply in Perry County?
sections.html: Owners aged 65 and over, along with those classed as totally disabled, can claim $49,100 off assessed value for 2025 and 2026. Applied to Perry's Census median owner-occupied value of $91,800, the taxable amount becomes $42,700. Ask the PVA's office for the form and bring proof of age.

sections.h2: What will a Perry County seller pay to record a deed?
sections.html:
The grantor owes Kentucky's transfer tax, a half dollar for every $500 of price in the deed, counting a partial $500 as whole (KRS 142.050), and the clerk takes it before accepting the instrument. On a $91,800 sale that is $92.00. Perry County Clerk's published minimums are $50 for a deed and $80 for a mortgage, and a deed adds $3 for each page after the fifth.

A title company will expect the current tax bill to be paid or prorated, a clerk's payoff if an earlier year went delinquent, and an in-care-of address on the deed for the next bill. The clerk's office can quote the total for any document, and staff there cannot run a title search, so an attorney or abstractor handles that step. The clerk's office also offers a free DocAlert service that emails owners when a deed or mortgage is filed in their name.

sections.h2: How do Census figures describe Perry County housing?
sections.html:
Home values here are the lowest of the three counties in a Census Bureau comparison.

  • Median owner-occupied value: $91,800, against $159,800 in Pendleton County and $112,000 in Pike County.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 70.4%, with median household income of $42,181.
  • Estimated 2025 population: 26,555, compared with 14,800 in Pendleton County and 54,721 in Pike County.
  • Mean commute of 24.8 minutes, and 47.4% of residents aged 16 and over in the civilian labor force.
  • 88.7% of households with broadband, and 14.8% of adults holding a bachelor's degree.

Perry's population fell 6.7% from the 2020 count of 28,473, and the 1940 census counted 47,828 residents. In 2020 the county had 13,213 housing units, 13.1% of them vacant, and QuickFacts shows 13,425 units in 2025 with zero building permits issued. Median rent is $798. Owner costs run $1,167 with a mortgage and $379 without one, and 24.5% of residents are in poverty.

sections.h2: How does Perry County's setting affect a sale?
sections.html:
Perry County covers about 343 square miles of the Appalachian coalfield and touches seven counties, from Breathitt to the north and Harlan to the south to Clay, Leslie, Owsley, Knott and Letcher. The legislature carved it out of Floyd and Clay counties and gave it, and its seat, the name of naval hero Oliver Hazard Perry. Coal and timber shaped its economy, and the Perry County museum keeps that story. The first post office opened in 1824 on the North Fork of the Kentucky River in a settlement then called Perry Court House. Public transit comes from the LKLP Community Action Partnership, with scheduled service in Hazard and links to Hindman, Hyden and Whitesburg, and the Hazard Herald covers local news.

Hazard Community and Technical College and the Hazard ARH Regional Medical Center lead local employment. Receipts from health care and social services totaled $507.7 million in 2022. Hazard and Buckhorn are incorporated cities, while Combs, Diablock, Jeff and part of Vicco are census-designated places. The county's own list of communities runs from Ary and Bulan to Rowdy, on Troublesome Creek, and Viper and Yerkes. Homes are served by two school systems: Perry County Schools, whose high school is Perry County Central, and Hazard Independent Schools, which cover the city. Buckhorn Lake State Resort Park, river access on the North Fork of the Kentucky River and a Trail Town designation draw outdoor visitors, and the county sits inside the first rural Promise Zone, named January 7, 2014.

Business owners should note that Perry County is a stacked occupational license county. The tax is 1% of wages and net profit, and anyone working inside Hazard city limits pays both the county and the city.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Perry County property tax in person?
faqs.a: At the Sheriff's Office, 124 East Main Street, Hazard, on weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00. Payments by post use box 7309, with checks written to Perry County Sheriff.

faqs.q: How much does the homestead exemption take off a Perry County home?
faqs.a: The deduction is $49,100 against assessed value for 2025 and 2026, which leaves a $91,800 home taxable at $42,700.

faqs.q: What transfer tax applies to a Perry County sale?
faqs.a: The rate is a half dollar for every $500 of the price stated in the deed, and the seller pays it. A sale at $91,800 owes $92.00.

faqs.q: Where do unpaid Perry County bills go after April 15?
faqs.a: They move to the county clerk as certificates of delinquency, with interest at one percent a month plus clerk and attorney fees.

faqs.q: Who decides a Perry County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: A local board of area property owners. The owner must meet the PVA first and file with the clerk by the workday after roll inspection closes.
